chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Husayn ibn Mukhtar, from Abu Hamza al-Thimali, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:
Indeed, the Master of this Command (al-Qa'im), if he were to appear, would receive from the people what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) received, and more.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Command, a title for the Mahdi (al-Qa'im)
key_terms.ظَهَرَ: To appear or emerge (referring to the Mahdi's reappearance)
key_terms.وَأَكْثَرَ: And more (indicating greater severity than the Prophet's trials)

ai.seo_question: What challenges will the Mahdi face upon his appearance according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Abu Hamza al-Thumali narrates from Imam al-Baqir that the Mahdi’s emergence will be marked by intense tribulations, exceeding even the Prophet’s trials, which underscores the continuity of divine testing in Shia eschatology. This comparison highlights the political and social resistance the Twelfth Imam will face upon his reappearance, framing his struggle as a culmination of prophetic history. The hadith serves to prepare the faithful for the inevitable opposition during the final phase of the occultation.
